_meta.purpose: Add-on to thaus_website_spec.json. Adds an INTERACTIVE hero graphic (cobalt node network reacting to mouse + scroll). Apply on top of the existing spec.
_meta.supersedes: There is NO hero video. The hero's right side uses this interactive canvas graphic instead. Ignore any earlier mention of a hero video.
instructionsToAgent: Build a HeroGraphic React component and mount it on the RIGHT side of the hero (desktop). On mobile it sits behind the hero content as a subtle, low-opacity layer.
Use the tsParticles approach below (primary). If a dependency issue arises, fall back to the custom canvas approach described in fallback.
The graphic must feel light, premium, and calm — subtle motion, never busy or distracting from the hero text.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion: render a static version (network drawn once, no animation, no interactivity).
Keep it performant: cap FPS, reduce node count on smaller screens, pause when off-screen or tab inactive.

placement.desktop: Right column of the hero (roughly 45-50% width). Text/CTAs on the left, graphic on the right.
placement.mobile: Full-bleed behind the hero content at ~30-40% opacity so text stays readable; reduce node count.
placement.zIndex: Sits below the hero text layer. pointer-events enabled only over the graphic area so hover works without blocking text/CTA clicks.
placement.background: Transparent — the page background (#0A0A0B) shows through. No box, no border.

primaryApproach.init: Initialize the engine once with loadSlim, then render <Particles id="hero-graphic" options={options} />.
notes: onHover 'grab' draws cobalt links from the cursor to nearby nodes — the classic constellation effect the user wants.
onHover 'parallax' gently shifts the whole field toward the cursor for depth.
Keep speed low (0.6) so it reads as calm, premium motion.

scrollBehavior.spec: Wrap the graphic in a motion.div. Use useScroll (target = hero section) and useTransform to map scroll progress to the graphic as the hero scrolls out of view.
scrollBehavior.note: This makes the graphic recede naturally as the user scrolls into the next section.

reducedMotion.detect: useReducedMotion() from framer-motion, or CSS/media query.
reducedMotion.fallback: Render the node network ONCE as a static frame: nodes + links drawn, no animation, no hover interactivity, no parallax. Slightly lower opacity. Ensures accessibility and no motion for sensitive users.

performance: Ensure the canvas cleans up on unmount.
Do not run heavy shaders; this is a lightweight 2D canvas effect.

fallbackApproach.when: Only if tsParticles causes build/version issues.
fallbackApproach.approach: Custom lightweight <canvas> component (~100-150 lines) in components/hero/HeroCanvas.tsx.
spec: Create N nodes (55 desktop / 30 mobile) with random positions and slow velocities on a transparent canvas sized to its container.
Each animation frame: move nodes, bounce off edges, draw nodes as small cobalt (#3B5BFF) dots.
Draw a line between any two nodes closer than 140px; line opacity scales with proximity (closer = more opaque), max ~0.22.
Track mouse position; draw brighter cobalt links (opacity ~0.5) from the cursor to nodes within 160px (the 'grab' effect).
Apply a subtle parallax: offset all nodes slightly toward the cursor (lerp, force ~28px).
Use requestAnimationFrame; cap to ~60fps; cancel on unmount; pause when tab hidden (visibilitychange) or off-screen (IntersectionObserver).
prefers-reduced-motion: draw one static frame and stop.

heroLayoutUpdate.note: Adjust hero from single-column to a two-column layout on desktop.
heroLayoutUpdate.desktop: Grid: left column = kicker + headline + subhead + CTAs + status line; right column = HeroGraphic. ~55/45 split.
heroLayoutUpdate.mobile: Single column: hero content on top; HeroGraphic as a subtle background layer behind it (low opacity), OR a short graphic block below the CTAs — prefer background layer.
heroLayoutUpdate.textContrast: If graphic overlaps text on mobile, add a subtle radial/linear dark overlay behind the text for readability.

buildInstructions: Create components/hero/HeroGraphic.tsx implementing the tsParticles options above.
Update the Hero section to a two-column layout and mount HeroGraphic on the right.
Wrap the graphic in a Framer Motion motion.div wired to useScroll/useTransform per scrollBehavior.
Verify performance (no jank), responsiveness, and that hovering the graphic never blocks the CTA buttons.
